subject: history_social
passage: In the Kula exchange of the Trobriand Islands, off the coast of Papua New Guinea, men made long canoe voyages to give and receive shell necklaces and armbands, which circulated in opposite directions around a ring of islands. The objects had little practical use, and no participant kept any of them permanently. Observers who expected trade to be driven by material gain found the system puzzling, but later anthropologists argued that its purpose was largely social: the exchanges established and maintained lasting partnerships between men on distant islands, so the value of a gift lay less in the object itself than in the relationship it ______.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The anthropologists say the exchanges "established and maintained lasting partnerships." A gift that keeps a relationship going "sustained" it.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text contrasts the Kula with trade driven by "material gain," so the gifts did not buy relationships.
explanation.B: Incorrect. To supplant is to replace. The gifts supported the partnerships; they did not take their place.
explanation.C: Incorrect. To sever is to cut off. The exchanges built and kept relationships rather than ending them.
explanation.D: Correct. The gifts kept partnerships going over time, matching "established and maintained lasting partnerships."
